Multiple outlets headline 'US imposes 130% tariff' or 'nearly 131%' WHILE NAMING HOA PHAT in the same sentence. 130.77% is the ALL-OTHERS rate. HOA PHAT'S RATE IS 121.97%, and it is lower precisely BECAUSE it was the mandatory respondent that participated. A separate petition figure of 117.61% also circulates and is neither the preliminary nor the final. FOUR NUMBERS ARE IN CIRCULATION FOR ONE CASE - 117.61 petition, 121.97 HPG preliminary, 130.77 all-others preliminary, and an unpublished final - and only one of them describes our holding. Same species as the AD-versus-CVD conflation logged 20:54 yesterday, one day later. WHAT THIS ALREADY TELLS US ABOUT FORECAST #10, registered now rather than after the rate lands. Provisional duties near 122% HAVE BEEN COLLECTED SINCE MARCH under the extension HPG itself requested. So HPG HAS ALREADY TRADED A FULL QUARTER UNDER THEM - and that quarter, Q2/2026 filed 29-Jul, printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51%. The commercial effect of losing US rebar is therefore ALREADY INSIDE THE REPORTED RUN-RATE rather than ahead of it. That is direct evidence for the forecast's stated reasoning - headline risk, not earnings risk - and it was available before the final. NOT SCORING YET: the forecast names the FINAL, and the final's numbers are not in hand. Recording the reasoning now means the eventual score cannot be constructed after the fact.
actuals._REVENUE_BLADE_IS_SPLITTING_2026_07_30: HPG RAISED DOMESTIC REBAR PRICES, and it qualifies my own 14:53 entry from yesterday. THE FACT: Hoa Phat Hung Yen raised high-grade rebar (CB400V, CB500V, B500B, Gr60) by 100 VND/kg ex-VAT in the North FROM 27-JUL. Reported as the FIFTH price adjustment of 2026, with several large mills raising from late July. Stated reason: input costs - iron ore, coking coal and SCRAP - staying high or trending up. Tier T5. WHAT IT QUALIFIES. The 29-Jul 14:53 entry read iron ore -5.3% m/m and coking coal -2.2% m/m as 'both cost blades easing, which is the one thing that would relieve HPG's H2 spread squeeze.' The Vietnamese trade view is the opposite: inputs anchored high or rising, which is WHY producers are raising prices. Both can be literally true - down slightly month-on-month, still high in level - but my framing was one-sided. THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS BEHAVIOURAL: mills raising prices five times in seven months is not what an industry does when its input costs are easing. SCRAP IS A THIRD INPUT THIS FILE NEVER TRACKED. The spread bridge models ore and coking coal only. Vietnamese sources name scrap alongside them as a driver of the increases. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, AND THE BRIDGE CANNOT SEE IT: THE REVENUE BLADE IS SPLITTING. Domestic HRC prices were reported FALLING on 13-Jul under import competition, while REBAR prices are being RAISED. HRC down, rebar up, at the same time. hpg-spread-bridge.md section 5 already lists this as its first honest limit - 'Product mix is ignored - HPG sells rebar as well as HRC, with different economics' - and that limit is now BINDING rather than theoretical. A bridge calibrated on a single HRC blade cannot represent a quarter where the two products move in opposite directions. NOTHING CHANGED. No branch, probability or weight. This is T5 and charter s2 forbids moving probs or exit_pe on T4-T6. It is recorded because H2 spread is the live variable on 16.8% of the book and because the direction of the revenue blade is now genuinely ambiguous rather than simply negative. Corroborating levels, both already consistent with this file: domestic HRC 14,000-14,350 VND/kg; iron ore ~98.02 USD/dmtu on 08-Jul against the 98.25 logged yesterday.
actuals._US_REBAR_FINAL_RATES_2026_07_30: THE FINAL RATES ARE PUBLISHED. Federal Register 2026-15438 (AD, Final Affirmative Determination of Sales at Less Than Fair Value) and 2026-15437 (CVD, Final Affirmative Countervailing Duty Determination), both dated 30-JUL-2026, applicable 30-Jul. Period of investigation 01-Oct-2024 to 31-Mar-2025. Tier T1 for the existence and dates; the RATES below are T5, from trade press, because federalregister.gov returns proxy 403 from this environment and the documents themselves could not be read. THE NUMBERS: FINAL DUMPING MARGINS FOR VIETNAM 128.53% TO 136.57%, with CASH DEPOSIT RATES ADJUSTED TO 123.49% TO 131.53% after offsetting export subsidies. Preliminary was 121.97% (Hoa Phat, mandatory respondent) to 130.77% (all others). SO THE FINALS CAME IN ABOUT 6.6pp HIGHER AT BOTH ENDS. WHICH END IS HOA PHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED, AND I AM NOT ASSERTING IT. The preliminary structure put the mandatory respondent at the LOWER rate, so 128.53% is the likely Hoa Phat figure and 136.57% the all-others - but that is an inference from structure, not a reading of the table. This is precisely the conflation warned about in _US_REBAR_IS_TWO_DUTIES_NOT_ONE_2026_07_29, and the warning applies to my own inference as much as to the press. USEFUL MECHANIC WORTH RECORDING: the CASH DEPOSIT RATE IS ~5pp BELOW THE MARGIN because of an export-subsidy offset between the AD and CVD cases. The deposit is what importers actually post, so it is the operative number for trade economics, not the headline margin. WHAT IT DOES TO THE THESIS: NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Provisional duties near 122% have been collected since March under the extension HPG itself requested. HPG has already traded a full quarter under them, and that quarter - Q2/2026, filed 29-Jul - printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51%. Moving a prohibitive duty from ~122% to ~129% changes nothing commercially: the trade was already uneconomic and the earnings effect is already inside the reported run-rate. US is ~3% of revenue. No branch, probability, weight or confidence changed.
actuals._REBAR_IS_NOT_OVER_2026_07_31: CORRECTION TO A STATUS I RECORDED YESTERDAY. The date-gate row was marked 'RESOLVED 30-Jul' after Commerce published its final AD and CVD determinations. COMMERCE'S PART IS RESOLVED. THE CASE IS NOT. WHAT REMAINS: the US INTERNATIONAL TRADE COMMISSION must make its FINAL INJURY DETERMINATION WITHIN 45 DAYS of Commerce's finals, so a vote around MID-SEPTEMBER 2026. ONLY AFTER AN AFFIRMATIVE ITC VOTE DO THE ORDERS ACTUALLY ISSUE. If the ITC finds no material injury, no duties are imposed at all and cash deposits collected under the provisional measures are REFUNDED. WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN FILING AWAY: THE REMAINING UNCERTAINTY ON REBAR IS NOW ASYMMETRIC TO THE UPSIDE, and nothing in this file models it. The DOWNSIDE - duties imposed at ~129% - is already inside the reported run-rate, because provisional duties near 122% have been collected since March and HPG's Q2 printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51% under them. The UPSIDE - an ITC negative, orders never issuing, deposits refunded - is not in any branch. ITC negatives in steel cases are uncommon but they are not unheard of, and the petition covers four countries so a split outcome by country is possible. NOT ADDING A BRANCH OR MOVING A PROBABILITY - both are judgment changes reserved for a human under charter s2. Recorded as a DATED CATALYST that belongs on the calendar, which is charter s1 test 3. FORECAST #10'S SCORE IS UNAFFECTED. It named the Commerce final explicitly ('~Jul 28 Federal Register') and that is what resolved it. The ITC vote is a separate event and does not reopen a scored forecast.
actuals._A_THIRD_FIGURE_FOR_THE_DIVESTMENT_GAIN_: OPEN-DECISIONS ITEM 13 MOVED FURTHER FROM RESOLUTION, NOT CLOSER, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY. A THIRD CANDIDATE FIGURE APPEARED THIS SWEEP: press states that in Q1/2026 APPROXIMATELY 3,800bn came from the capital-transfer at the PHO NOI urban project. Tier T5, and explicitly approximate ('khoang'). THERE ARE NOW THREE NUMBERS FOR ONE LINE: 4,123 as carried in q1_divestment_gain; 4,010 as implied by q1_npat 9,056 minus q1_core_npat 5,046; and ~3,800 from this sweep. 3,800 is 7.8% below the file's figure and 5.2% below the implied one - TOO FAR TO BE A ROUNDING OF EITHER. IT WEAKENS THE EXPLANATION THIS FILE PREFERRED. The existing note offers 'likely explanation: 4,123 is PRE-tax and 4,010 is post-tax, implying 113bn of tax = a 2.7% effective rate, well below the 20% CIT - possible but not obvious'. A COMPETING READING NOW HAS SUPPORT: that ~3,800 IS PHO NOI ALONE while 4,123 is TOTAL divestment or other income including roughly 300bn of something else. On that reading the 113bn gap is COMPOSITION, not tax, and the tax story is unnecessary. THE FILE'S OWN H1 NON-STEEL RECONCILIATION assumed the whole 4,123 was Pho Noi ('Pho Noi one-off 4,123 + agriculture ~648 = 4,771'), so that reconciliation inherits the same ambiguity. NEITHER READING IS ESTABLISHED AND NEITHER IS ADOPTED. WHAT IT COSTS, QUANTIFIED. q1_core_npat / q1_volume_mt is the CALIBRATION ANCHOR of the spread bridge - conversion_usd_t 114 was solved backwards to reproduce it. The three candidates give: gain 4,123 -> core 4,933 -> anchor 1.644m/t; gain 4,010 -> core 5,046 -> anchor 1.682m/t; gain 3,800 -> core 5,256 -> anchor 1.752m/t. THE ANCHOR RANGE IS 1.644 TO 1.752m/t, A 6.5% SPREAD, and the new figure moves it in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION from the alternative previously considered - the file had only ever contemplated the anchor being LOWER than 1.68, and 3,800 makes it HIGHER. The bridge's whole cost structure is calibrated off this one number. A CHECK THAT DOES PASS, recorded so it is not re-litigated: 4,123 is a Q1 figure, not an H1 one. Q1 9,056 + Q2 6,424 = 15,480 = stated H1 exactly, so the quarters are clean and the gain sits inside Q1. NOTHING CHANGED. q1_divestment_gain is NOT edited - three candidate values is a reason to escalate, not to pick. The resolving document is HPG's Q1 or H1 financial statement note on other income, which this environment cannot reach.
actuals._HPG_HAD_NO_BALANCE_SHEET_AND_THERE_IS_A: HPG'S BLOCK CONTAINED NOTHING ON DEBT, BORROWINGS, CAPEX, CASH FLOW OR INVENTORY - ZERO HITS ON ALL FIVE. That is 16.8% of the book with a proposed ADD of +3.2pp, mid-way through DUNG QUAT 2, one of the largest industrial capex programmes in Vietnam. COMPARE KDH, WHOSE BLOCK CARRIES BORROWINGS, INVENTORY, OPERATING CASH FLOW AND D/E. THE DEVELOPER GOT A BALANCE SHEET; THE CAPEX-HEAVY STEELMAKER DID NOT. AND THE WHOLE WEEKEND WENT INTO HPG'S SPREAD - ore, coal, HRC, the bridge, the calibration anchor - WHICH IS A PURE P&L EXERCISE. A capex-heavy cyclical's risk is at least as much balance sheet as margin. NOW ON FILE: BORROWINGS OF MORE THAN 90,617bn AT END-Q1/2026. CONSTRUCTION IN PROGRESS ROSE SHARPLY TO OVER 10,328bn AND Q1 INVESTING CASH FLOW WAS MINUS 2,921bn. One outlet frames it as Hoa Phat 'straining to balance profit, cash flow and enormous debt pressure'. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS AN ACCOUNTING INFLECTION THE BRIDGE CANNOT SEE. Sources state that ONCE DUNG QUAT 2 REACHES FULL CAPACITY, HOA PHAT NO LONGER CAPITALISES INTEREST INTO CONSTRUCTION IN PROGRESS, SO ALL INTEREST EXPENSE FLOWS STRAIGHT INTO THE INCOME STATEMENT. THE SPREAD BRIDGE MODELS ORE, COAL, HRC AND A CONVERSION COST. IT DOES NOT MODEL INTEREST AT ALL. So a step-change in reported earnings can arrive with the spread completely unchanged, and nothing in this file would anticipate it. SCALE, WITH THE UNKNOWN NAMED. At 90,617bn of borrowings a blended 5-7% implies 4,531-6,343bn of annual interest, which is 19-27% OF THE CORE BASE BRANCH OF 23,336bn. WHAT SHARE WAS BEING CAPITALISED IS UNKNOWN AND IS NOT GUESSED - the impact is the newly-expensed portion, not the whole. The range is recorded to show the order of magnitude of the line the model omits, NOT as an estimate of the hit. THIS IS THE KDH LESSON'S MIRROR. At KDH a ONE-OFF GAIN masked a core collapse and made reported profit look better than the business. At HPG a CAPITALISED COST BECOMING AN EXPENSED ONE would make reported profit look worse than the business. BOTH ARE PRESENTATION EFFECTS THAT THE OPERATING MODEL CANNOT SEE, and this file has now been caught by the first one. TWO TRAPS HANDLED. (1) ENTITY: the same coverage gives 'total assets 5,239.3bn' and 'inventory +23.5% to 546.8bn' - the source itself labels these CONG TY PHAT TRIEN NONG NGHIEP HOA PHAT, THE AGRICULTURE SUBSIDIARY, NOT HPG. HPG's total assets are two orders of magnitude larger. NOT LOGGED AS HPG. (2) VINTAGE: a separate item gives 'borrowings over 65,000bn with idle cash near 35,000bn'. That is a DIFFERENT AND OLDER VINTAGE than the 90,617bn, so THE TWO ARE NOT MERGED AND NO NET DEBT IS COMPUTED ACROSS THEM. ESCALATED, NOT MODELLED - adding an interest line to the bridge is a rebuild and human-only under charter s4.
actuals._CAP_NOW_CROSS_CHECK_2026_08_02_1153: CAP_NOW IS 7.6% TOO LOW - mu_raw +15.1% -> +6.4%, a 8.8pp move. BELOW the 10pp threshold, so trigger 3 does NOT fire, recorded as material rather than escalated. HPG issued 767m shares in MAY 2026, taking charter capital 76,755bn -> 84,430bn (8,443m shares); the file's inputs imply 7,800.3m and therefore predate an action that has already settled. Note this compounds with the two known HPG input problems already on file - the missing FX line and the missing interest line in the spread bridge. Not retuned.
actuals._HPG_IS_A_PETITIONER_IN_A_LIVE_TRADE_CAS: HPG IS 16.8% OF THE BOOK AND IS AN ACTIVE PARTY TO A VIETNAMESE TRADE-DEFENCE CASE THAT THIS FILE HAD NO RECORD OF. With Formosa Ha Tinh it petitioned MoIT over Chinese circumvention of the HRC anti-dumping duty via wide-format coil, and won a TEMPORARY 27.83% duty on 1,880-2,300mm HRC from China - Decision 612/QD-BCT, effective 17-APR-2026. See _regulatory.decision_612_qd_bct. TWO THINGS FOLLOW THAT ARE NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. (1) A FINAL DETERMINATION IS PENDING because the measure is provisional, and its date is not established - an unlogged dated catalyst on a 16.8% position, and the second live trade case on this name alongside the US rebar ITC vote due mid-to-late September. (2) THE PROTECTION HAS NOT HELD THE PRICE: three months after it took effect domestic HRC was still falling with import competition reported as INCREASING, and HPG cut its own August offer ~US$34/t. So this does NOT rehabilitate the spread case, and it must not be read as bear-evidence-cancelled. NOTHING MODELLED. Confidence NOT moved: no model input changed, the bridge's HRC input is HPG's own offer which already embeds this measure, and HPG separately has an unresolved cap_now defect (item 25) that would make any confidence move uninterpretable.
actuals._THE_MISSING_INTEREST_LINE_IS_NOW_SIZED_: THE SPREAD BRIDGE'S MISSING INTEREST LINE HAS BEEN FLAGGED TWICE WITHOUT A NUMBER. IT NOW HAS ONE, AND IT IS BIG. HPG'S FINANCIAL DEBT REACHED A RECORD 98,530bn AT 30-JUN-2026, UP 9% FROM END-2025, driven mainly by SHORT-TERM borrowing for working capital. Q1/2026 financial costs roughly DOUBLED to ~1,868bn, of which INTEREST EXPENSE WAS OVER 1,333bn - about 15bn PER DAY (1,333/90 = 14.8, which checks). SIZED AGAINST THE THING THE WHOLE MODEL TURNS ON. Q1 volume is 3.0m tonnes (H1 6.5 minus Q2 3.5), so INTEREST IS ~444,000 DONG PER TONNE = 0.444m/t. The bridge's core NPAT/tonne branches are bear 1.25, base 1.60, bull 1.85, with Q1 actual core at 1.68. SO INTEREST RUNS AT 24% OF THE BULL BRANCH, 28% OF BASE AND 35.5% OF BEAR. Annualised at the Q1 run-rate it is 5,332bn, or 24.2% of the 22,000bn FY profit target. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN - THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. NPAT is struck AFTER interest, so interest is already INSIDE the observed core NPAT/tonne; this does not mean the model double-counts or omits it arithmetically. WHAT IT MEANS IS THAT THE BRIDGE HAS NO LINE THAT RESPONDS TO IT. Volume and spread move across the three branches; interest per tonne is held constant by construction. With debt UP 9% in six months and financial costs DOUBLING year on year, holding it constant is an assumption that the evidence now contradicts - and it bites hardest in the bear branch, where it is over a third of the whole figure. IT ALSO COMPOUNDS WITH THE USD/VND FINDING. The dong's central rate hit a record 25,338 on 1-Aug. IF any material share of this debt is USD-denominated, a depreciating dong raises the domestic-currency cost of servicing it on top of the volume increase. THE CURRENCY MIX OF HPG'S DEBT IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT ASSUMED - it is the next cheap check, and it is one line off the filed balance sheet. A FIGURE REJECTED IN THE SAME SOURCE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-ADOPTED. The summary carrying the debt number also stated H1 after-tax profit of 'over 10,539bn, completing 67% of the annual plan'. THAT IS NOT THIS YEAR. The file's 15,480bn is corroborated THREE WAYS: it is 70.4% of the 22,000bn target as reported; Q1 9,056 + Q2 6,424 = 15,480 EXACTLY; and 15,480 against H1/2025's 7,600 is +104%, matching the filed +103%. 10,539 at 67% implies a plan near 15,730bn, which is a 2025-vintage plan (FY2025 actual was 15,515bn). The revenue figure in the same summary - 108,870bn, +47% - IS the correct H1/2026 one, so the source mixes a current revenue with a prior-year profit. SECOND TIME IN TWO HOURS THAT A SUMMARY HAS BUNDLED A TRUE CURRENT FACT WITH A STALE ONE. NOTHING MODELLED - branch construction is human-only under charter section 4. Confidence NOT moved: no input changed, and this argues for re-deriving the branches rather than scaling them.
actuals.interest_capitalisation_ceased: after Dung Quat 2 reached full capacity, interest is no longer capitalised into construction-in-progress and is expensed instead
actuals._THE_INTEREST_STEP_IS_STRUCTURAL_NOT_CYC: RAN THE CURRENCY-MIX CHECK NAMED AT 02:53. IT DID NOT ANSWER THAT QUESTION - recorded as still open - BUT IT RETURNED THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE INTEREST STEP, WHICH IS WORTH MORE. THE MECHANISM: AFTER DUNG QUAT 2 REACHED FULL CAPACITY, HOA PHAT NO LONGER CAPITALISES BORROWING COSTS INTO CONSTRUCTION-IN-PROGRESS AS IT DID BEFORE. While DQ2 was being built, interest on the debt funding it was capitalised into the asset and never touched the income statement. Now it is EXPENSED. THAT IS WHY Q1/2026 INTEREST IS DOUBLE THE SAME PERIOD OF 2024 AND 14% ABOVE Q4/2025. THIS IS A STRUCTURAL, PERMANENT, ONE-DIRECTION CHANGE IN THE P&L - NOT A CYCLICAL SWING - AND THE 14% QUARTER-ON-QUARTER STEP SAYS IT IS STILL WORKING THROUGH. THE DEBT PATH, AND ALMOST ALL OF IT IS Q2. Total borrowings and finance leases were ~90,600bn at end-MAR (about 69% SHORT-TERM, ~62,800bn) against 98,530bn at end-JUN. Implied end-2025 is ~90,394bn from the +9% YTD already on file. SO DEBT WAS ESSENTIALLY FLAT IN Q1 (+206bn) AND ROSE 7,930bn IN Q2 (+8.8%). The borrowing is recent and short-dated. AND HERE IS THE PART THAT CHANGES HOW THE BRIDGE SHOULD BE READ. INTEREST PER TONNE IS INVERSELY GEARED TO VOLUME, SO IT PUNISHES THE BEAR BRANCH SPECIFICALLY. At a full-year interest run-rate near 5,682bn (Q1 actual plus three quarters at the debt-adjusted Q2 rate of ~1,450bn): bear FY volume 13.5m t gives 0.421m/t = 33.7% of a 1.25m core NPAT/tonne; base 14.5m t gives 0.392m/t = 24.5% of 1.60m; bull 15.5m t gives 0.367m/t = 19.8% of 1.85m. THE BEAR CASE IS HIT TWICE - LOW VOLUME AND, BECAUSE OF THAT SAME LOW VOLUME, THE HIGHEST INTEREST BURDEN PER TONNE. Yesterday's 02:53 note established that no branch RESPONDS to interest; this establishes that the direction it would respond in is ADVERSE TO THE DOWNSIDE, which is the branch a risk model exists to get right. STATED FAIRLY, THE OTHER SIDE: interest per tonne FALLS as DQ2 volume ramps - 0.421 to 0.367 across the branches - WHICH IS PRECISELY THE POINT OF THE INVESTMENT. This is not a story about a broken balance sheet; it is operating leverage working in both directions, and the model currently shows neither. THE CURRENCY QUESTION IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT GUESSED. Two searches failed to establish the currency mix of the debt. WHAT IS BOUNDED: Q1 financial costs of 1,868bn less interest of 1,333bn leaves 535bn OF NON-INTEREST FINANCIAL COST. For a company importing iron ore and coking coal in USD with a record-high dong, FX is the obvious candidate - AND IT IS ONLY A CANDIDATE. 535bn is an upper bound on any FX loss in the quarter, not a measurement of one. STILL THE NEXT CHEAP CHECK, still one line off the filed statement. NOTHING MODELLED; branch construction is human-only. Confidence NOT moved - this sharpens OPEN-DECISIONS item 28 rather than changing an input.

spread_bridge_2026_07_26._COKING_COAL_CORRECTED_2026_07_28: CORRECTION, and it REVERSES the direction of the 27-Jul conclusion. THE ERROR: _BOTH_INPUTS_VERIFIED_2026_07_27 states 'Coking coal SPOT 228 (PHCC FOB Australia, -24% MoM from 238.9 on 10-Jul)'. Those two clauses contradict each other on their own figures - 238.9 to 228 is -4.6%, not -24%. Nothing caught it because the sentence was never divided into itself, which is exactly the failure CONSISTENCY-AUDIT.md was written about. WHAT THE PRICE ACTUALLY IS (T5, two independent sources this sweep): PHCC FOB Australia was 238.9 on 10-Jul, with an early-July bid of 241 for an Aug 1-10 laycan, against a June 2026 average of 244.39 (range 242-249). So roughly 238-241 in mid-July - about 1-2% below the June average. Coal is broadly FLAT, drifting slightly down. It is not collapsing. The 228 in this file is not corroborated by anything found since. WHAT THIS KILLS: that note's conclusion that 'coal falling 24% in a month is a live UPSIDE risk' and that 'at coal 200 the spot case reaches 1.21m/t, essentially the bear branch'. Coal is not heading to 200. The upside argument does not hold. WHAT IT DOES TO THE NUMBER, using this model's own gearing of 0.14 VND m/t per US$10 of coal: from the 27-Jul spot case of 0.83m/t, coal at 238.9 gives 0.68m/t, at 241 gives 0.65m/t, at the June average 244.39 gives 0.60m/t. If iron ore is also nearer 99-103 CFR Qingdao than the 97.70 SGX figure in file, the case falls to 0.49-0.62m/t. EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS FURTHER BELOW THE 1.25m/t BEAR BRANCH, NOT CLOSER. The 27-Jul note concluded the gap to bear was 'a third of what it looked like'. That was too generous. The spread at spot is worse than that note said, though still not as bad as the original mis-logged 0.36m/t. THIRD COMMODITY-PRICE ERROR in this workstream, after logging a Fitch iron-ore FORECAST as spot. Not applied to any branch: bear/base/bull stay 1.25/1.60/1.85, because changing them is a judgment call reserved for a human. The TIMING note still holds - Q2 burns Q1 inputs, so this lands in Q3.
spread_bridge_2026_07_26._HRC_BENCHMARK_TRAP_2026_07_28: WARNING for future runs. A commodity search this sweep returned 'HRC 1169.08 USD/T'. That is NOT the benchmark this model uses and MUST NOT be substituted for the 539 in file. This model prices Asian/Vietnamese HRC, which runs roughly 500-560/t; 1169 is almost certainly US Midwest HRC (CME). Same product name, different market, more than double the level. Charter section 3's ENTITY check applies to commodity benchmarks exactly as it does to company financials.
spread_bridge_2026_07_26._FX_IS_UNLABELLED_2026_07_28: The bridge carries FX 26,300 described only as 'VND/USD market rate'. On 28-Jul there are two very different market rates: the SBV CENTRAL rate at 25,306 - an all-time high, passing the 25,298 set 25-Aug-2025 - and the FREE MARKET at 26,400-26,420. A 4.4% gap. The 26,300 in file sits 0.4% below the free market and 3.9% above the central rate, so it appears to be a free-market figure, but nothing says so. HOW MUCH THIS MATTERS DEPENDS ON SOMETHING THE BRIDGE ALSO DOES NOT STATE: whether HPG's realised HRC price is treated as USD-linked or VND-fixed. If USD-LINKED, FX multiplies a USD margin of (539 - 522) and largely CANCELS - the choice between the two rates is worth about VND 0.019m/t, trivial. If VND-FIXED, FX hits only the USD cost side and the choice is worth VND 0.576m/t - 85 to 96% of the 0.60-0.68m/t spot margin and 46% of the 1.25m bear branch. REALITY IS IN BETWEEN: roughly 80% of HRC volume is domestic and priced in VND, tracking import parity with a lag and imperfectly - and the Formosa price cut suggests domestic prices are currently set by competition rather than by FX. So partial pass-through. But the bridge does not say, which means it cannot be interrogated on the question, and that is the defect. NOT CHANGED. No branch moves and nothing here is an escalation. Recorded because it is the same species as the day's other findings - an input whose LABEL decides the answer - and it sits on the live variable days before HPG reports. spread_bridge_2026_07_26._FX_RATE_PINNED_2026_07_29: ANSWERS the open question in _FX_IS_UNLABELLED_2026_07_28, which asked which of several 'market rates' applies to HPG's imports. SECOND FACT, and it is a constraint rather than a price: the SBV band is +/-5% around the central rate, so floor 24,041 and ceiling 26,571. Techcombank's sell rate of 26,530 sits 41 dong below that ceiling - 0.16%. With the central rate at an all-time high, commercial rates are pinned against the cap. FURTHER DONG WEAKNESS HAS TO COME THROUGH THE CENTRAL RATE, not through the market, because there is no room left in the band. spread_bridge_2026_07_26._ANCHOR_IS_CONTAMINATED_BY_NON_STEEL_202: THIRD problem found with the 1.682m/t calibration anchor, and this one has a clear direction. Hoa Phat AGRICULTURE (HPA) filed H1/2026 today: revenue 3,379bn, NPAT 648bn, 64% of its full-year plan, implying an FY plan near 1,012bn. HPG Group itself is still unfiled. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: this bridge models HPG as a STEEL business - NPAT per tonne times tonnes - and its conversion_usd_t of 114 was SOLVED BACKWARDS so the bridge reproduces a Q1 core anchor of 1.682m/t (5,046bn over 3.0mt). But that 5,046bn is GROUP profit and includes non-steel earnings. SIZING WITH AGRICULTURE ALONE: HPA runs about 324bn a quarter, so (5,046 - 324) / 3.0mt = 1.574m/t - 6.4% below the anchor. And agriculture is only one non-steel segment; real estate, appliances, pipe and galvanised sheet also sit outside the 3.0mt basket, so a true steel-only margin is lower still. DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: an anchor that is too HIGH means the solved conversion cost is too LOW, so the bridge UNDERSTATES steel costs and OVERSTATES the spread at every price point. That is the same direction as the other two anchor problems - the 113bn core/one-off reconciliation gap (_RECONCILIATION_FLAG_2026_07_28) and the FX rate sitting 0.87% below the bank sell rate (_FX_RATE_PINNED_2026_07_29). Three separate issues, all pushing the modelled spread the same way: too generous. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: HPA's ownership percentage, so how much of the 648bn is attributable to HPG shareholders is unknown; and whether HPA's profit is inside the 5,046bn 'core' figure at all, which depends on how that core number was constructed. Both read off the segment note in the group statement. NOT APPLIED. Re-solving the conversion cost on an inferred non-steel share would replace one unverified anchor with another. The group statement lands within a day and carries the segment note that settles it.

hpg._HPA_SIZED_AND_THE_PHO_NOI_QUESTION_CLOS:
STRUCTURE SWEEP, SECOND PASS. Every open sub-question from the 15:53 entry is now answered, and one hypothesis I formed while writing it turned out FALSE.

THE STRUCTURE. HPA charter capital 2,850bn after the IPO (from 2,550bn), so 285.0m SHARES AT PAR 10,000. 30m shares placed at 41,900, gross ~1,257bn, NET 1,206bn after ~50bn of issue costs. HPG HOLDS 242.2m SHARES = 84.999%. Ten foreign investors hold 1.163%; 964 small holders make up the rest.

THAT CLOSES THE PHO NOI QUESTION DEFINITIVELY, AND IT CLOSES IT AS A NO. At 85% retained THERE IS NO DECONSOLIDATION, so HPA CANNOT BE THE SOURCE OF THE 4,123bn GAIN this file excludes from fy26e_npat. The 15:53 entry named the possibility and refused to infer it; the refusal is now discharged with a number rather than left hanging. A minority sell-down inside a consolidated subsidiary raises consolidated equity and creates a 15% NCI. IT DOES NOT CREATE A P&L GAIN.

A HYPOTHESIS I FORMED AND THEN KILLED. Reading 'dinh gia cao nhat nganh' - the highest valuation in its sector - I expected HPA to have been floated at a PREMIUM multiple to its parent, which would have been a governance point. IT WAS NOT. HPA'S FY2025 NPAT IS 1,600bn (+55%, 22% ABOVE PLAN). AT THE IPO PRICE THE COMPANY WAS WORTH 11,942bn - A P/E OF 7.46x AGAINST HPG'S OWN pe_ttm OF 7.51x. THE TWO ARE THE SAME MULTIPLE TO WITHIN 0.6%. 'Highest in the sector' is a statement about AGRICULTURE peers, not about the parent, and I nearly read it as the latter.

WHAT THE MARKET HAS DONE SINCE, AND THE DATE IS CONVENIENT. HPA TRADED AT 32,000 ON 22-JULY-2026, DOWN 23.6% FROM THE 41,900 IPO. Market capitalisation 9,120bn; HPG'S 84.999% IS WORTH 7,752bn, WHICH IS 4.41% OF HPG'S 175,614bn. 22-JULY IS WITHIN DAYS OF THE ~20-JULY DATE ITEM 2 INFERS FOR THIS FILE'S OWN PRICES, so for once a peer price and the book's prices are roughly the same vintage.

AND HPA'S OWN TRAJECTORY CORRECTS A CHARACTERISATION IN THIS FILE. hpg.evidence says 'STEEL IS 68% OF H1 PROFIT and 93% of revenue - NON-STEEL IS OVERWHELMINGLY THE PHO NOI ONE-OFF'. THAT IS NOT RIGHT. HPA IS RECURRING, DIVIDEND-PAYING AND SEPARATELY PRICED. H1/2026 revenue 3,379bn and NPAT 648bn; annualised 1,296bn, i.e. MINUS 19% on FY2025 - and HPG's 85% share of that annualised figure is ~1,102bn, WHICH IS 4.7% OF THE 23,336bn BASE BRANCH. SMALL, BUT NOT A ONE-OFF, AND DECLINING. NOTE ALSO THE PLAN: HPA GUIDES FY2026 NPAT OF 1,005bn, DOWN 37% ON 2025 - so the company itself expects a material fall, and H1's 648bn is 64% of that already-reduced plan. THE ANNUALISED RUN-RATE BEATS THE PLAN WHILE FALLING YEAR-ON-YEAR; both are true and the file should hold both.

A CASH FLOW THE FILE HAD NO RECORD OF. HPA PAYS A 30% CASH DIVIDEND FOR 2026 PLUS THE REMAINING 21% OF ITS 2025 DIVIDEND, AND HPG IS DUE 569bn OF IT. Eliminated on consolidation, but it is REAL CASH TO THE PARENT, and it lands on a parent carrying record financial debt of 98,530bn with a newly structural interest line (open item 28). 15% leaks to minorities. Small; recorded because the file's HPG cash picture had no non-steel inflow in it at all.

AND THE CROSS-HOLDING THAT UPGRADES THIS MORNING'S FINDING. VIETCAP BOUGHT ABOUT 12 MILLION HPA SHARES - 39% OF THE ENTIRE OFFERING - AS PRINCIPAL. AT 41,900 THAT IS ~502.8bn OF VCI'S OWN MONEY IN A SUBSIDIARY OF HPG. At 15:53 this file recorded the VCI/HPG link as a REVENUE CORRELATION and said so carefully. IT IS MORE THAN THAT: IT IS A DIRECT EQUITY POSITION. SIZED AGAINST VCI: the position is ~2x VCI's entire Q2 NPAT of 251bn, and at 32,000 the paper loss is 118.8bn - 47% OF ONE QUARTER'S PROFIT. THE FILE'S PROP-BOOK NOTE READS 'prop book -430bn on FPT/MWG/KDH'. HPA IS A FOURTH NAME AND IT IS NOT ON THAT LIST.

WHAT MUST NOT BE CONCLUDED FROM THAT, AND THIS IS THE DISCIPLINE POINT. THE 118.8bn IS NOT A Q3 HIT. The IPO was JANUARY and the 32,000 print is 22-JULY, so MOST OR ALL OF THAT DECLINE FALLS IN H1 AND WOULD ALREADY BE INSIDE VCI'S REPORTED H1 MARKS. Also unestablished: whether VCI still holds the position, at what size, and under which classification. WHAT IS FAIR TO SAY: VCI's Q3 needs PBT of 594bn - 2.19x its Q2 actual - and it carries an undisclosed-size position in a name down 23.6% from cost. That RAISES the variance around the kill criterion; it does not move its central estimate.

NOTHING MODELLED. No branch, probability, price, weight or confidence moved on HPG or VCI. NO SUM-OF-THE-PARTS IS ATTEMPTED: HPA is CONSOLIDATED, so its earnings are already inside HPG's reported numbers and adding a stake value to a P/E-based valuation would double-count.

On MBB the branches are contradicted FROM BELOW, so raising confidence would amplify branches that understate a good quarter - it would move E[r] up toward a number that is still too low. The defect is the same one-scalar-two-meanings problem in both, but here the charter already forbids the move, so no deviation is needed. actuals._THE_RATIO_IS_FLATTERED_BY_LOAN_GROWTH_2: THE ASSET-QUALITY NUMBER THAT MATTERS IS NOT THE RATIO. Group 3-5 bad debt rose 27% TO NEARLY 17,800bn. The NPL RATIO went 1.42% -> 1.45%, which reads as almost nothing. IT READS AS ALMOST NOTHING BECAUSE THE DENOMINATOR GREW 13.2% YTD. A 27% rise in the numerator against a 13.2% rise in the denominator produces a 3bp move in the ratio, and the 3bp is what the coverage reported. CROSS-CHECK PASSES: 1,220,000bn of customer loans x 1.45% = 17,690bn against the stated 'nearly 17,800'. RECORDED AS A NEAR-MATCH, NOT A MATCH - 'gan 17.800' is a rounded phrase and 17,690 is a derived figure, so they agree in magnitude and are not the same number. PERIOD OF THE 27% IS NOT STATED AND IS NOT ASSUMED. If YTD, end-2025 bad debt was ~14,016bn on loans of ~1,077,700bn, an NPL ratio of ~1.30% - so the honest description of the half is 1.30% -> 1.45%, not 1.42% -> 1.45%. If YoY the picture differs. The YTD reading is the more plausible because every other comparison in the same coverage is against end-Q1 or end-2025, but it is NOT ESTABLISHED and is flagged rather than asserted. WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT DO TO THE SCORED READ. Calibration forecast #4's pre-registered read said MBB would MISS ON CREDIT COST. It was scored WRONG on 31-Jul because MBB BEAT OUTRIGHT, which was the explicitly stipulated falsifier. THAT SCORE STANDS AND IS NOT REVISITED. Finding credit deterioration in the balance sheet AFTER scoring does not partially rescue a read that was wrong about the outcome - that is precisely the retrofitting the pre-registration existed to prevent, and the temptation to do it is the reason this paragraph is here. WHAT IT DOES ADD, SEPARATELY: coverage ROSE from 92.24% to 93.63% while bad debt rose 27%, so RESERVES GREW FASTER THAN NPLs - roughly 29% - to a stock of about 16,666bn. MBB PROVISIONED SUBSTANTIALLY AND STILL GREW PBT 40%. That is the closest this file has got to the missing H1 provisioning charge after four attempts, and it is a BOUND ON THE BALANCE, NOT THE P&L FIGURE: reserve stock change equals provisioning charge minus write-offs, and write-offs are unknown. THE H1 PROVISIONING EXPENSE REMAINS UNFOUND.

BUT Q2 CIR IS 27.54% AGAINST Q1'S 24.94%, WORSE BY 2.60pp QUARTER ON QUARTER. Cost efficiency improved year-on-year and deteriorated sequentially, and a reader given only the first number would not know the second. Same shape as the VCI lesson from 26-Jul: '+36% YoY' and '-26% QoQ' described one quarter and every source reported the first.

actuals._THE_CASH_DIVIDEND_AND_THE_RIGHTS_ISSUE_: AN ARITHMETIC IDENTITY THIS FILE HELD ALL THE PIECES OF AND NEVER DIVIDED. MBB's 15% stock dividend is 12,082bn, WHICH IMPLIES CHARTER CAPITAL OF 80,547bn. Ten percent of that is 8,055bn - EXACTLY the cash dividend paid from 17-JUL. And the rights issue of 805.5m shares at par 10,000 RAISES 8,055bn, THE SAME NUMBER AGAIN. All three figures were already in this file separately; none had been divided into the others. SO THE CASH GOING OUT AND THE CASH COMING BACK IN ARE IDENTICAL. Both are 10% of charter capital at par. FOR A HOLDER WHO TAKES UP RIGHTS IN FULL, THE NET CASH FLOW ACROSS THE TWO EVENTS IS ZERO - and after the 5% PIT on the cash dividend it is slightly NEGATIVE, about -403bn across the register, because the dividend is taxed and the subscription is not discounted for that. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a claim that the package is economically neutral. IT IS NOT. The rights are priced at 10,000 against a market price of 22,050 - 45.4% of market, a 54.6% DISCOUNT - so the round trip converts taxed cash into shares at well under half price. The correct reading is that MBB's headline '25% distribution' is, for a participating holder, LARGELY A ROUND TRIP IN CASH TERMS whose value sits in the subscription discount rather than in the distribution. A holder who does NOT take up gets the cash, pays the tax, and is diluted at 10,000. AND ONE RECORD DATE COVERS BOTH. Press states the final registration date for exercising rights under BOTH plans - the 15% stock dividend and the 805.5m-share offering - falls at the SAME time point, per the legal requirement. So this is ONE dated catalyst, not two, and when it lands it lands together. A DATE WAS OFFERED AND IS NOT LOGGED. A search summary attached '14 August' to this, but described it as the record date for '2024 DIVIDENDS' - a YEAR that does not match, and the summary itself hedged with 'appears to be'. That is the tenth instance this week of a plausible date attached to the wrong period, and it is exactly the shape of the MBB 10-Jun/10-Jul error already on file. NO RECORD DATE IS RECORDED. The 15% and the rights remain undated pending a disclosure that states the year.

mbb._NO_DRIVER_MODEL_2026_07_28: MBB is NOT built by run.py. fy26e_npat 28,000/30,500/33,000 is asserted directly. INVERTING IT - the check the audit called for - the branches turn out to be COHERENT, which is worth saying plainly since the audit implied they might not be. At a 0.80 NPAT/PBT ratio they imply FY26 PBT of 35,000 / 38,125 / 41,250 against a company plan of 39,400-39,500. So base sits just below guidance and bull just above: a sensible spread AROUND the plan, not a number pulled from nowhere. Against npat_ttm 28,065 the branches are flat / +8.7% / +17.6% on trailing profit. WHAT REMAINS WRONG is not the level, it is that no driver produces it. TCB's base comes from credit +18%, NIM 3.3%, credit cost 0.5% - move any one and the branch moves. MBB's base comes from nothing, so it cannot be stress-tested: if SBV changes MBB's quota or NIM compresses, there is no lever to pull. That is the real cost of the gap, and it is a reason to BUILD the model, not to distrust the number. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT TONIGHT. The H1 statement lands within about 48 hours and will supply loans, NIM, CIR and NPL as filed actuals. Building a driver block now from press summaries - one of which already mislabelled the period - then rebuilding it Thursday would waste the work and risk anchoring on the wrong numbers. Charter section 6 date-gating logic applies to depth work too. Pre-registered read below instead.
mbb._PRE_REGISTERED_H2_READ_2026_07_28: Written BEFORE the H1 print. Each fy26e_npat branch implies a required SECOND-HALF PBT, so the H1 actual translates straight into which branch is still live. Required H2 growth versus H1: | H1 17,000 -> bear +5.9%, base +24.3%, bull +42.6% | H1 18,000 -> bear -5.6%, base +11.8%, bull +29.2% | H1 18,440 -> bear -10.2%, base +6.8%, bull +23.7% | H1 19,000 -> bear -15.8%, base +0.7%, bull +17.1% | H1 20,000 -> bear -25.0%, base -9.4%, bull +6.2% | H1 21,000 -> bear -33.3%, base -18.5%, bull -3.6%. If Q2 lands near the 8,812 estimate, H1 is ~18,440 and the base branch needs +11.7% on the Q2 quarterly run-rate. STATED FAIRLY: Vietnamese bank profit is seasonally second-half weighted, because credit quota gets used late and fee income concentrates at year-end, so +11.7% is not alarming on its own. ONE DAY OF OIL IS ONE DAY and it is recorded as one - but the MECHANISM WAS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE DATA, which is what makes noting it legitimate rather than opportunistic. IT BEARS ON THE LIVE CPI FINDING: 4.45% is still ~0.95pp above risk.py's 0.035 threshold, and a fuel-led reversal would widen that gap rather than close it. NOTHING MODELLED. No rate or oil price is a model input; these are context for two conclusions already on file.
_market._ISM_SERVICES_JULY_2026_THE_TWO_HALVES_P:
THE GATED ITEM LANDED. ISM SERVICES FOR JULY, RELEASED TODAY 05-AUG AT 10:00 ET (21:00 ICT), READ 53 MINUTES AFTER RELEASE. THE PREVIEW ARTICLE PUBLISHED THIS MORNING WAS NOT USED - only the release.

THE NUMBERS. HEADLINE SERVICES PMI 54.1 against 54.0 in June, the 25TH CONSECUTIVE MONTH OF EXPANSION - essentially flat, and a shade below the 'expected to accelerate' framing of the previews. PRICES PAID 70.3, AGAINST CONSENSUS 65.0 AND 67.7 PRIOR - UP 2.6 ON THE MONTH AND 5.3 ABOVE CONSENSUS. EMPLOYMENT 47.4, AGAINST CONSENSUS 51.2 AND 51.2 PRIOR - DOWN 3.8 ON THE MONTH, 3.8 BELOW CONSENSUS, AND INTO CONTRACTION.

THE INFLATION LEG IS CORROBORATED OUT OF SAMPLE, AND THIS FILE HAS A HISTORY HERE THAT MAKES THAT WORTH STATING PRECISELY. On 03-Aug this file claimed ISM Manufacturing at 55.6 'restores the FX support', WITHDREW the claim when the market did not reprice hawkishly, then REINSTATED ONLY THE NARROWER FUNDAMENTAL CLAIM resting on Prices Paid 71.1 - and flagged the reinstatement as the suspicious move it looked like. TODAY IS AN INDEPENDENT TEST OF THAT NARROWER CLAIM, FROM A DIFFERENT SURVEY COVERING A DIFFERENT AND MUCH LARGER PART OF THE ECONOMY. MANUFACTURING PRICES PAID 71.1; SERVICES PRICES PAID 70.3. BOTH ABOVE 70, BOTH ABOVE CONSENSUS. THE INFLATION-PRESSURE CLAIM IS CORROBORATED. THE MARKET-REACTION CLAIM REMAINS WITHDRAWN AND IS NOT REVIVED BY THIS.

AND THE OTHER HALF GOES THE OTHER WAY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. SERVICES EMPLOYMENT AT 47.4 IS CONTRACTION, AND A WEAK LABOUR MARKET IS EXACTLY WHAT PRODUCES CUTS. MANUFACTURING EMPLOYMENT WAS REPORTED BACK IN EXPANSION ON 03-AUG. THE TWO SURVEYS NOW DISAGREE ON LABOUR WHILE AGREEING ON PRICES. SO THE RELEASE IS STAGFLATIONARY IN SHAPE - PRICES UP, EMPLOYMENT DOWN - AND THAT CONFIGURATION SUPPORTS NEITHER THE HAWKISH NOR THE DOVISH READ CLEANLY. I AM NOT CLAIMING THIS STRENGTHENS THE FX-SUPPORT ARGUMENT. IT STRENGTHENS ONE LEG AND WEAKENS THE OTHER, AND SAYING SO IS THE CORRECTION OF THE 03-AUG ERROR RATHER THAN A REPEAT OF IT: THAT ERROR WAS READING ONE COMPONENT AND DECLARING A CONCLUSION.

A PRE-REGISTRATION FOR FRIDAY, WHICH MAKES IT SCOREABLE. THE US JULY EMPLOYMENT REPORT LANDS 07-AUG, ALREADY GATED. SERVICES IS THE LARGER SHARE OF US EMPLOYMENT, SO A SERVICES EMPLOYMENT INDEX FALLING 51.2 -> 47.4 RAISES THE PROBABILITY OF A WEAK PAYROLL PRINT. THAT IS THE DIRECTION I EXPECT AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE EVENT. THE LIMIT, STATED WITH IT: ISM EMPLOYMENT SUB-INDICES ARE POOR MONTH-TO-MONTH PREDICTORS OF PAYROLLS - they are diffusion indices over firms, not headcount - so this is a tilt, not a forecast, and a strong payroll print WOULD NOT FALSIFY the inflation leg.

THE VIETNAM CHAIN, AND IT IS WORSE THAN EITHER DIRECTION ALONE. This repo's chain runs Fed -> US rates -> USD/VND -> SBV's two-sided constraint, with USD/VND at a record 25,338 and CPI near 4.4%. A CLEANLY HAWKISH US PRINT TIGHTENS THE FX SIDE; A CLEANLY DOVISH ONE EASES IT. A STAGFLATIONARY ONE MAKES THE FED'S PATH LESS PREDICTABLE, AND UNPREDICTABILITY IS WORSE FOR AN FX-CONSTRAINED CENTRAL BANK THAN A KNOWN DIRECTION. NO POSITION, BRANCH OR CONFIDENCE MOVES ON THIS. It is macro context, and this file's own rule - established on circular_25 and applied six times today - is that a change in the environment is not evidence about a forecast.

circular_25_2026_tt_nhnn.amends: Circular 22/2019/TT-NHNN, prudential limits and safety ratios
circular_25_2026_tt_nhnn._WHAT_IT_DOES: The SBV raised the maximum share of SHORT-TERM funding a bank may deploy into MEDIUM- AND LONG-TERM LENDING from 30% to 40%. It also brings deposits from other credit institutions into the safety ratio, with carve-outs for escrow, dedicated-capital deposits, State Treasury demand deposits and 80% of State Treasury term deposits. Published in the government gazette (congbao.chinhphu.vn, vanban.chinhphu.vn) and carried by the Vietnam Banks Association, so this is T1 official regulator text, not press about it. One published estimate puts the headroom created at around 1,000,000bn of additional medium- and long-term capacity system-wide, with REAL ESTATE named as a beneficiary.
circular_25_2026_tt_nhnn._WHY_IT_MATTERS_HERE: This is the single largest loosening of the constraint that actually binds Vietnamese bank loan growth, and it lands on 71.8% of this book - banks 51.5% plus KDH 20.3%. ON THE BANKS. Every bank model here forecasts CREDIT GROWTH as the primary driver, and the notes on VPB and MBB both frame H2 as demanding: VPB needs about +22.5% in H2 on one reading of its contradictory credit pair, and MBB needs roughly +15% to +22% depending on which FY target is right. Part of what made those look demanding was an unstated assumption that funding constraints bind as they did under the 30% cap. FROM 01-JUL THEY BIND LESS - and 01-Jul is exactly the start of the H2 those requirements describe. The H2 hurdle for VPB and MBB is therefore more achievable than the notes on file imply. This is the SECOND finding today pointing that way for MBB, after the credit trajectory was anchored at 14:53. ON KDH. Property is named as a direct beneficiary. Easier long-term bank funding helps developers refinance and helps their buyers get mortgages. KDH carries debt up 51% to 15.3tn with its land bank fully pledged, so its sensitivity to term-funding availability is high. NOT RETUNING ANYTHING. Charter s5: where new evidence bears on a THESIS rather than a NUMBER, it is escalated, not quietly worked into the branches. No probability, branch or weight changed. CONFIDENCE ALSO HELD, and the reason matters. This is T1, and charter s2 permits T1 to raise confidence to 0.90 - but confidence measures how well evidenced OUR SPECIFIC FORECASTS are, and a favourable change in the operating environment does not validate a number that still fails its own cross-check. VPB's two credit fields still contradict each other. A better environment for a figure we cannot verify is not better evidence for that figure.
circular_25_2026_tt_nhnn._HOW_THIS_WAS_MISSED: Issued 22-Jun, effective 01-Jul, in force for FOUR WEEKS and for the whole of the quarter this book has been analysing, and this repo had no record of it until 29-Jul 17:53. It surfaced only as a side clause in a market-recap search run for a different lane. THE SAME SPECIES AS THE 28-JUL LESSON about HPG's half-year volume disclosure sitting unlogged for three weeks: the lanes hunt for NEWS, and a circular published in the government gazette is not news - it is dated, scheduled, primary and findable. Lane 5 nominally covers 'SBV/MoF circulars'; in practice nothing was checking the gazette on a schedule. This is a process gap, not an information gap.

_regulatory._ITC_DATE_CHECKED_AND_HELD_AND_A_STALE_D: THE ~MID-SEPTEMBER ITC DATE ON FILE IS CONFIRMED, AND A CONFLICTING 'AUGUST' IS DISARMED BEFORE A FUTURE SWEEP WALKS INTO IT. decision_45_2026_qd_ubnd.subject: 2026 land-price adjustment coefficient (he so K)
decision_45_2026_qd_ubnd.formula: K = K1 x K2 x K3; for 2026 K1 = 1 and K3 = 1, so K reduces to K2, set by project type
decision_45_2026_qd_ubnd.note: THIRD DATED REGULATION THIS WEEK FOUND IN FORCE WITH NO RECORD IN THIS REPO, AND THE SECOND EFFECTIVE 01-JUL-2026. HCMC issued Decision 45/2026/QD-UBND setting the 2026 land-price adjustment coefficient, effective 01-JULY-2026 under Resolution 254/2025, which required every province and city to publish a K coefficient by that date. IT HAS BEEN IN FORCE FOR A MONTH. Searching this repo for 'land-use fee', 'bang gia dat', 'he so K', 'Land Law' and '254/2025' returns ZERO HITS in assumptions.json and ZERO in monitoring-log.md. Lane 5 explicitly covers 'HCMC approvals, LAND-FEE/LEGAL CHANGES, developer bonds' and that lane item has never produced anything. THE PATTERN, THIRD TIME IN FOUR DAYS: HPG's half-year volume disclosure sat unlogged three weeks (found 28-Jul); Circular 25/2026/TT-NHNN sat unrecorded four weeks, EFFECTIVE 01-JUL (found 29-Jul); this, ALSO EFFECTIVE 01-JUL, was never recorded at all. THE 29-JUL LESSON SAID 'regulator gazettes now join recurring operating disclosures as dated catalysts to be checked on their own cadence' - AND IT DID NOT EXTEND, because it was written about SBV circulars and this is a MUNICIPAL land decision, a different regulator bearing on a different holding. A lesson scoped to the regulator that produced it does not generalise on its own. NOTE ALSO that two separate instruments took effect on the SAME DATE, 01-Jul-2026, and both were missed - that date should have been watched as a cluster. WHY IT BEARS ON THE BOOK. Land-use fee is the single largest cost input for a Vietnamese residential developer, and it is computed as the land price table multiplied by K. HCMC's NEW LAND PRICE TABLE took effect 01-JAN-2026, built on 'market principles' under the 2024 Land Law, raising land prices across most areas with the largest increases reported at EIGHT TIMES; central districts rose modestly while fast-developing areas in the merged Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau units rose far more. KDH IS 20.3% OF THE BOOK with inventory above 23,000bn - land awaiting development - and Gladia and Clarita are exactly the kind of unlaunched or absorbing projects on which a land-use fee obligation crystallises. THE DIRECTION IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND THE OBVIOUS READING IS NOT TAKEN. 'Land prices up, therefore bad for developers' is available and this file is not taking it. Press frames Decision 45 as intended to THAO GO VUONG MAC - remove obstacles - in property procedures and in the financial obligations of individuals and businesses, because an unpublished K coefficient had itself been blocking valuations and approvals. So a higher table raises fees while a published K unblocks stalled process, and this file cannot net the two. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN, STATED SO IT IS NOT GUESSED: KDH's project-specific K2 values, and WHICH OF ITS PROJECTS HAVE ALREADY SETTLED THEIR LAND-USE FEE - fees are typically assessed at assignment or conversion, so projects already paid are unaffected regardless of the new table. Without both, any number put into the model would be invented. ESCALATED, NOT MODELLED: no branch, probability, weight or confidence touched.

circular_08_2026_tt_nhnn.subject: 20% of State Treasury TIME DEPOSITS countable as capital in the LDR calculation
circular_08_2026_tt_nhnn.note: FOURTH DATED REGULATION FOUND IN FORCE WITH NO RECORD IN THIS REPO, AND THE OLDEST YET - THREE MONTHS. Issued MAY 2026, it lets banks count 20% of State Treasury time deposits as capital when computing the LOAN-TO-DEPOSIT RATIO, expanding lending capacity. Zero hits for 'LDR', 'Circular 08' or '08/2026' anywhere in assumptions.json before this entry. IT RELAXES THE EXACT CONSTRAINT THIS FILE SPENT THE NIGHT FLAGGING. Within the last six hours this repo recorded that TCB's loans outgrew deposits 2.2x in H1 (10.4% vs 4.8%) and that MBB grew customer loans 13.2% YTD, and read both against the 31-Jul finding that interbank funding cost rose 30-59bp across July. THE IMPLIED WORRY WAS THAT THE FUNDING GAP WOULD BIND. Circular 08 loosens the ratio that would bind it. THE WORRY IS NOT WITHDRAWN - a looser ratio does not make funding cheaper, and the interbank price moved regardless, which is the same distinction drawn for Circular 25 on 31-Jul: A CIRCULAR RELAXES A RATIO, IT DOES NOT LOWER A PRICE. But the constraint is looser than the night's entries implicitly assumed, and that should be on the record beside them.

credit_quota_exemptions_2026.subject: Lending excluded from the credit room / real-estate credit for 2026
credit_quota_exemptions_2026.scope: 25 commercial banks may exclude additional social-housing, industrial-zone and EPZ lending from real-estate credit; 18 projects of 3 private economic groups excluded from the credit room
credit_quota_exemptions_2026.note: THIS NAMES THE MECHANISM BEHIND A GAP THIS FILE RESOLVED TWO HOURS AGO BY INFERENCE. At 03:53 the TCB credit-versus-loans question was settled using the company's own phrasing - standalone credit +14.3% 'INCLUDING INFRASTRUCTURE AND SOCIAL-HOUSING LOANS THAT ARE EXCLUDED FROM CREDIT LIMITS' against customer loans +10.4%. THE POLICY BEHIND THAT CLAUSE IS NOW IDENTIFIED AND DATED: SBV permits 25 commercial banks to exclude additional social-housing, industrial-zone and export-processing-zone lending, and has removed 18 projects of 3 private economic groups from the room entirely. An upgrade from a company's characterisation to a named instrument. AND IT BREAKS CROSS-BANK COMPARABILITY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. TCB reports TWO rates and says which is which. MBB reports customer loans +13.2% YTD. VPB reports parent credit +24.6%. THIS FILE DOES NOT KNOW WHICH OF THOSE CONTAIN QUOTA-EXEMPT LENDING AND WHICH DO NOT. Every cross-bank credit-growth comparison made this week - including 'MBB's version of VPB's problem is milder' - implicitly treated the rates as one comparable quantity. THEY ARE NOT NECESSARILY THE SAME MEASURE. That does not invalidate the per-bank H2 arithmetic, which was computed against each company's own reported base and its own branches; it invalidates comparing the three rates to each other. SCALE CONTEXT WORTH HOLDING: SBV projects SYSTEM credit growth of ~15% for 2026. Against that, MBB targets 30-35%, VPB's FY plan implies ~34% (962,000 -> 1.29 quadrillion) and TCB's branches are 16-20%. TWO OF THE THREE BANKS IN THIS BOOK PLAN TO GROW CREDIT AT MORE THAN TWICE THE SYSTEM RATE. Individual quotas vary by design and healthier banks get more, so this is not an objection - but it does mean both plans depend on continued preferential allocation or heavy use of exemptions, and neither dependency is modelled anywhere. A PERIOD TRAP DISARMED IN PASSING: the widely-circulated 'PRIME MINISTER ORDERS SBV TO PILOT REMOVING THE CREDIT ROOM FROM 2026' is dated AUGUST 2025, not now, and the pilot REMAINS UNDER DEVELOPMENT. A future sweep will find those articles and they are a year old.

circular_29_2026_tt_nhnn.subject: Amends Circular 39/2016/TT-NHNN on lending by credit institutions to customers
circular_29_2026_tt_nhnn.grandfathering: agreements signed before 15-Aug-2026 continue under the old rules; any amendment after that date must comply with the new ones
circular_29_2026_tt_nhnn.tier: T1/T2 instrument; substance from T5 press
circular_29_2026_tt_nhnn.note: THE FIRST REGULATION THIS REPO HAS FOUND BEFORE ITS EFFECTIVE DATE RATHER THAN AFTER, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ENTRY. Circular 29/2026/TT-NHNN was ISSUED 30-JUN-2026 and takes effect 15-AUG-2026 - TWO WEEKS FROM NOW. Compare the four found in the past three days: Circular 25/2026 (four weeks late), HCMC Decision 45/2026 (one month), Circular 08/2026 (THREE months), and the credit-quota exemptions (undated). ALL FOUR WERE FOUND ONLY AFTER SOMETHING ELSE MADE THEM RELEVANT. THE BACK-SWEEP COMMITTED ONE HOUR AGO WAS RUN IMMEDIATELY AND THIS IS ITS FIRST RESULT. The lesson written at 06:53 was 'SBV and MoF circulars get a monthly back-sweep of the preceding quarter, not a search when a thesis needs one'. Running it once turned a pattern of retrospective discovery into a dated catalyst with two weeks of warning. That is the difference between writing a lesson and applying it, and it is recorded because the previous four show what the alternative costs. WHAT IT CHANGES, AS FAR AS IS ESTABLISHED. Three named areas: DEBT-HANDLING PROCEDURES, SMALL-VALUE LOAN LIMITS, and THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR ELECTRONIC LENDING. Small-value loans are now quantified, at not more than 200,000,000 VND for people's credit funds - a threshold that does not touch our banks directly. Agreements signed before 15-Aug run on under the old rules, but ANY AMENDMENT after that date must comply with the new ones, so the transition reaches existing books through restructurings. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IS NOT GUESSED. The amendments are known by ARTICLE NUMBER (Art.1 cl.3, Art.2 cl.13, Art.8 cl.6(b), Art.18 cl.4, Art.22 cl.2(h)) and by press characterisation, NOT by text - thuvienphapluat's full-text page returns proxy 403, the SIXTH host to refuse this session. Article 8 of Circular 39 is the list of purposes credit institutions may NOT lend for, so an amendment there is potentially the most consequential of the five, BUT THIS FILE HAS NOT READ IT and will not infer its content from its location. One outlet headlines the circular as good news for borrowers; whether that is neutral, positive or negative for LENDER margins is a different question and is unanswered. WHY IT PLAUSIBLY MATTERS HERE, STATED AS A REASON TO WATCH RATHER THAN A FINDING: the three areas are retail and consumer lending, and this book holds VPB (which contains FE CREDIT), MBB (which contains MCREDIT) and TCB, 51.5% between them. The electronic-lending framework is the piece most likely to matter to a digital-first lender. NOTHING MODELLED, no confidence moved, no branch touched.

_regulatory._THE_SOURCE_THAT_MAKES_THE_BACK_SWEEP_RE: MORE USEFUL THAN ANY SINGLE CIRCULAR: A RECURRING SOURCE WITH A PREDICTABLE CADENCE. luatvietnam publishes a monthly digest titled 'Chinh sach moi ve tai chinh ngan hang hieu luc thang [N]/2026' - NEW FINANCE AND BANKING POLICIES TAKING EFFECT IN MONTH N. It is forward-looking by construction, which is exactly what every one of this week's four late catches lacked. FIVE MISSED OR LATE REGULATIONS IN FOUR DAYS SHARE ONE CAUSE: the lanes hunt for things that HAPPENED, and a circular gazetted on a known date never 'happens' in that sense. The fix is not a better search query, it is a SOURCE WITH A CALENDAR. Recorded here so the next sweep does not have to rediscover the method along with the content. Also worth checking on the same cadence: NHNN publishes an annual programme of the circulars it intends to issue - 18 for 2026, seven of them planned for Q2 - which makes the pipeline itself checkable in advance rather than only the output. ALSO FLAGGED, NOT PURSUED THIS SWEEP: Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC guides the Corporate Income Tax Law and Decree 320/2025. This model assumes a 20% effective CIT throughout - MBB's Q1 checks at exactly 0.80 NPAT/PBT - so a CIT guidance change would touch ALL EIGHT names at once rather than one sector. NOT READ, and no tax assumption has been altered on the basis of a title.

circular_31_2026_tt_nhnn.subject: Financial leasing by GENERAL finance companies and FINANCIAL LEASING companies; replaces Circular 26/2024/TT-NHNN
circular_31_2026_tt_nhnn.change: brings PROPERTY RIGHTS - software, data, exploitation rights, intellectual property - into the list of assets eligible for financial leasing
circular_31_2026_tt_nhnn.tier: T5 press on a gazetted circular
circular_31_2026_tt_nhnn.note: SECOND SBV INSTRUMENT EFFECTIVE 15-AUG-2026, WHICH CONFIRMS THAT DATE AS A CLUSTER. Circular 29/2026 (lending) was logged an hour ago on the same effective date. The 31-Jul lesson that EFFECTIVE DATES CLUSTER - written after 01-Jul turned out to carry both Circular 25/2026 and HCMC Decision 45/2026 - now has a second instance, and this time the cluster is FOURTEEN DAYS AHEAD rather than a month behind. SCOPE CHECKED, AND IT RESOLVES NEGATIVE, WHICH IS THE USEFUL ANSWER. The circular governs 'cong ty tai chinh TONG HOP' (GENERAL finance companies) and 'cong ty cho thue tai chinh' (FINANCIAL LEASING companies). This book reaches two finance companies through its banks: FE CREDIT (VPB) and MCREDIT (MBB). Both appear to be CONSUMER finance companies rather than general or leasing ones - MCredit's legal name is 'Cong ty Tai chinh TIN DUNG TIEU DUNG TNHH MB Shinsei', consumer credit written into the name itself, and FE Credit is 'Cong ty Tai chinh TNHH MTV Ngan hang Viet Nam Thinh Vuong', whose business descends directly from VPBank's consumer credit division. Vietnam's Law on Credit Institutions separates GENERAL finance companies from SPECIALISED ones, and consumer finance is a specialised type that does not conduct financial leasing. HEDGED DELIBERATELY: THIS IS READ FROM COMPANY NAMES AND PRESS DESCRIPTIONS, NOT FROM THE LICENCES. A licence is the only thing that settles which category a company holds, and this environment cannot reach the SBV register. The finding is 'probably out of scope', not 'out of scope'. RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE RESULT SO IT IS NOT RE-RAISED. A regulation that LOOKED like it touched two holdings' subsidiaries was checked and probably does not. That is the fourth negative deliberately logged in two days, after the CORE trade case, the KDH ownership headlines and the KDH listing-site ASP route - each recorded because the next sweep would otherwise spend the same budget reaching the same dead end.

_regulatory._AUGUST_2026_BACK_SWEEP_REMAINDER_2026_0: WHAT ELSE THE AUGUST DIGEST CONTAINS, AND WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Also effective in August 2026: a decree setting administrative penalties up to 100 MILLION VND for individuals and 200 MILLION for organisations, described as tightening market discipline. ITS DOMAIN IS NOT ESTABLISHED - the summary does not say whether it covers securities, banking, or something unrelated - so it is recorded as a loose end rather than as a finding, and no holding is claimed to be affected. ONE ITEM CROSS-CONFIRMS SOMETHING ALREADY LOGGED: the digest describes 'RAISING THE SMALL-LOAN CEILING TO STIMULATE CREDIT' among August's economic policies, which is the small-value-loan provision of Circular 29/2026 recorded an hour ago, now framed as a STIMULUS measure rather than a technical definition. Consistent, and it slightly strengthens the reading that the circular's direction is expansionary. ACCESS NOTE: luatvietnam's own August digest page returns proxy 403, the SEVENTH host to refuse this session, so the digest was read through search summaries rather than directly. The source remains the right one to check monthly - see _THE_SOURCE_THAT_MAKES_THE_BACK_SWEEP_REPEATABLE_2026_08_01 - but a human with unblocked access would get a complete list where this sweep got a partial one.
_regulatory._THE_THREE_BANK_STOCK_ISSUES_ARE_NOT_THE: THE SET IS COMPLETE AND THE ANSWER IS COUNTERINTUITIVE. After pinning VPB's label an hour ago, the same check was run on the other two flags written in the same form - the 29-Jul lesson that when one stale flag is found, every other flag of the same shape gets checked in the same sweep. ALL THREE ARE NOW PINNED AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME INSTRUMENT. TCB 60%, over 4.28bn shares, charter capital +42,876bn: BONUS SHARES ISSUED FROM OWNER'S EQUITY (co phieu thuong). A capital restructuring, NOT a dividend distribution. Separately its 7% cash (4,960bn) IS from undistributed profit and is a real dividend. VPB 26.04%, 2.06bn shares: STOCK DIVIDEND FROM RETAINED EARNINGS, amended in July from an owner's-equity bonus issue approved at the 22-Apr AGM. MBB 15%, over 1.2bn shares, 12,082bn: STOCK DIVIDEND FROM UNDISTRIBUTED ACCUMULATED PROFIT of 21,234bn at 31-Dec-2025, part of a 25% total distribution worth 20,137bn of which 8,055bn is the 10% cash. SO THE LARGEST OF THE THREE STOCK ISSUES IS THE ONE THAT IS NOT A TAXABLE DISTRIBUTION, AND THE TWO SMALLER ONES ARE. That is the opposite of what 'TCB is paying 67%' suggests, and it is exactly the distinction that disappears when all three are recorded as 'a big stock issue pending'. SIZED ON THE FILE'S OWN TAX_DIVIDEND = 0.05, par basis, at on-file prices: TCB 0.12% of price (cash only), VPB 0.62%, MBB 0.57%. Weighted by position that is 0.042 / 0.062 / 0.037pp, TOTALLING 0.141pp OF THE WHOLE BOOK from three names that are 51.5% of it. THREE CAVEATS, STATED BECAUSE THE NUMBER LOOKS MORE SOLID THAN IT IS. (1) Vietnamese PIT on stock dividends is generally COLLECTED ON DISPOSAL, not at issuance, so this is a DEFERRED liability rather than a current cost - it reduces realised proceeds whenever the holder sells, which for a long-term holder may be years away. (2) The 5% rate is the file's own assumption in cfa.py and has NOT been verified against current law this sweep; the draft MoF decree carried as TAX_GAINS_DRAFT = 0.20 shows the regime is in flux. (3) Prices are the undated ones OPEN-DECISIONS item 2 already flags. WHAT IT ADDS TO ITEM 3: that item asks a human to set a cash_yield convention. The answer now needs THREE cells, not one - cash dividend, stock dividend, and bonus issue - because the book holds one of each and they are taxed differently. Recording all three as 'pending corporate action' was hiding a real difference between the two largest positions.

circular_121_2020_tt_btc.subject: Total margin lending by a securities company must not exceed 200% of OWNER'S EQUITY
circular_121_2020_tt_btc.also: Quyet dinh 87/QD-UBCK (2017) governs the margin trading regime; per-stock loan ratios run 10-50% by ticker
circular_121_2020_tt_btc.tier: T1/T2 instrument, named from T5 sources
circular_121_2020_tt_btc.note: THE RULE THE FILE HAS BEEN USING WITHOUT NAMING, PLUS THE NUMBER IT NEVER COMPUTED. This repo already applies a 2.0x cap - VCI's note reads 'margin 16,644 / 0.97 = equity 17,159' against 'a 2.0x cap', and VPX's derives 'ceiling >=71,177 => equity >=35,588' from it. NEITHER NAMED THE INSTRUMENT. It is CIRCULAR 121/2020/TT-BTC: total margin debt of a securities company may not exceed 200% OF OWNER'S EQUITY. Per-stock lending ratios run 10-50% depending on the ticker, under Decision 87/QD-UBCK (2017). 'Margin rules 91/102' is named in the lane definition and returns ZERO hits in this repo; the binding instrument is 121/2020, so the lane text may be pointing at the wrong circulars. AND HERE IS WHAT WAS NEVER COMPUTED: TCBS'S OWN UTILISATION. On this file's figures - TCX market cap pe_ttm 20.3 x npat_ttm 4,050 = 82,215bn, at P/B 2.49 - implied EQUITY is ~33,018bn, so the regulatory ceiling is ~66,036bn. TCBS'S MARGIN BOOK OF 51,500bn IS THEREFORE ~1.56x EQUITY, OR 78% OF THE REGULATORY CAP, with headroom of roughly 14,500bn. THE THREE BROKERS SIT AT VERY DIFFERENT UTILISATIONS AND THE FILE HAD ONLY LOOKED AT TWO: VCI 0.97x, VPX ~1.07x, TCBS ~1.56x. THE FILE HAS CRITICISED VCI FOR NOT USING ITS CAPACITY - 'unused capacity that stays unused in the best conditions on record is a description of the business, not an option on it' - and has treated VPX's >33,000bn of unused room as its REAL BULL CASE, better than the CAEX option. IT NEVER NOTICED THAT TCX IS THE ONE ACTUALLY LEVERED. WHICH REFRAMES THE TCX CASE WITHOUT CONTRADICTING IT. TCX ranks first on expected return and earns ~31% of H1 PBT from margin interest on that 51,500bn book. Those earnings come from a balance sheet that is MORE THAN THREE QUARTERS DRAWN AGAINST ITS REGULATORY LIMIT, so the margin line cannot grow much faster than equity does. The same fact that makes VCI look inert makes TCX look constrained - and neither reading was available while only two of the three were measured. NOTE WHAT DOES NOT RELIEVE IT: TCB's 60% BONUS ISSUE MOVES RESERVES INTO CHARTER CAPITAL AND DOES NOT INCREASE TOTAL OWNER'S EQUITY - and in any case it is the PARENT's equity, not TCBS's. Capacity at TCBS moves on retained earnings or a capital injection, neither of which is on file. STATED WITH ITS CAVEAT: TCX's equity here is DERIVED from pe_ttm x npat_ttm / P/B, not read from a balance sheet, and npat_ttm cross-checks have already failed twice in this repo (VCI 25.2% off, VPX 9-27% off). SO 1.56x IS AN ESTIMATE BUILT ON FILE FIGURES, NOT A FILED NUMBER. It is directionally robust - TCBS would need equity above 25,750bn merely to be legal at 51,500bn - but the precise utilisation needs TCBS's reported equity. ESCALATED, NOT MODELLED.

_regulatory._THE_FIRST_MOIT_INSTRUMENT_IN_THIS_FILE_: SEVENTH INSTANCE OF THE LATE-REGULATION SPECIES, AND THE ONE THAT SHOULD STING MOST. Decision 612/QD-BCT has been IN FORCE SINCE 17-APR-2026 - three and a half months - and there is no record of it anywhere in this repo: zero hits for 'kho rong', 'wide-format', '1880', 'lo hong thue' or 'loophole' in either the log or this file. WHY IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN CAUGHT: the 31-JUL calibration lesson, written after the FOURTH such miss, said the fix was to 'name the regulators per holding rather than the category' and named them explicitly - 'SBV and MoF for the banks and brokers, HCMC/provincial People's Committees and MoNRE for KDH, MoIT and USITC/Commerce for HPG'. THIS BLOCK NOW CONTAINS THIRTEEN INSTRUMENTS AND UNTIL THIS ENTRY NOT ONE OF THEM WAS FROM MoIT. The lesson named the regulator and no sweep ever queried it. The monthly back-sweep that was set up covers SBV/MoF gazettes via luatvietnam's banking-finance digest, which by construction cannot surface a trade-defence decision. WHAT THE MEASURE IS. Vietnam already levied 23.01-27.83% anti-dumping duty on Chinese HRC of width below 1,880mm. Chinese exporters shifted to WIDE format - 1,880-2,300mm - which fell outside the scope. Wide HRC imports from China ran ~650,000t in H1/2025, ABOUT 15 TIMES the prior-year period. NOTE THE PERIOD: that is H1/2025, a YEAR OLD, and the current run-rate is NOT established here. Hoa Phat and Formosa Ha Tinh petitioned MoIT; the preliminary investigation found circumvention through 'insignificant modification of goods already subject to trade defence measures'; Decision 612 applies 27.83% to the wide band across 24 HS codes, excluding carbon above 0.30% and plate 10mm or thicker. IT IS TEMPORARY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FORWARD. 'Thue tam thoi' - a provisional measure - so a FINAL determination is still to come and is A DATED CATALYST THIS FILE DOES NOT CARRY. Its date is not established here. HPG IS A PETITIONER, NOT A BYSTANDER, so this is also a governance/positioning fact about the company. AND THE HONEST READING CUTS AGAINST THE OBVIOUS ONE. The naive read is 'protection granted, domestic HRC prices supported, bullish for the spread'. THE PRICE EVIDENCE ON FILE SAYS OTHERWISE. Three months AFTER the duty took effect, domestic HRC was still falling under import pressure - a 13-JUL report has domestic HRC down with import competition INCREASING - and HPG then cut its own August offer by ~US$34/t with Formosa cutting ~US$40/t across August-September. SO THE MEASURE CLOSED A CHANNEL; IT DID NOT HOLD THE PRICE. Both facts are true at once and the file should carry both. NOTHING MODELLED - no trade-policy input exists in the spread bridge, and the bridge's HRC input is already pinned to HPG's own offer, which prices this measure in by construction.

_regulatory._THE_INDIA_TERMINATION_IS_THE_MECHANISM_: RAN THE MoIT BACK-SWEEP CREATED ONE HOUR AGO. IT IMMEDIATELY PRODUCED THREE MORE INSTRUMENTS, ALL ABSENT FROM THIS REPO, AND ONE OF THEM EXPLAINS THE 14:53 FINDING RATHER THAN ADDING TO IT. THE 14:53 PUZZLE WAS: a 27.83% anti-circumvention duty took effect 17-Apr-2026 and domestic HRC KEPT FALLING under rising import competition, with HPG cutting its August offer ~US$34/t. The entry concluded 'the measure closed a channel; it did not hold the price' and could not say why. NOW IT CAN. DECISION 1959/QD-BCT, 04-JUL-2025, DID TWO THINGS IN ONE DOCUMENT. It imposed the OFFICIAL Chinese HRC anti-dumping duty of up to 27.83% FOR FIVE YEARS - running to roughly 04-JUL-2030 unless replaced, extended or revoked, which is long-dated support this file did not have - AND IT TERMINATED THE INVESTIGATION INTO INDIAN HRC. THE REASON FOR THE INDIA TERMINATION IS THE PART THAT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT 'INDIA WAS FOUND NOT TO BE DUMPING'. The investigation was terminated because Indian imports during the investigation period were LESS THAN 3% OF TOTAL IMPORT VOLUME - the de minimis NEGLIGIBILITY threshold. That is a VOLUME test, and it was measured over a DATED window (the AD20 investigation period, case initiated July 2024). SO THE IMPORT CHANNEL THAT REMAINS OPEN IS INDIA'S, AND THIS FILE HAS BEEN CARRYING EVIDENCE OF IT WITHOUT THE EXPLANATION. 'Indian landed at 535' was logged as spread bear-evidence on 26-Jul and the file never knew Indian HRC carries NO anti-dumping duty at all. Chinese HRC: 27.83% for five years, plus the wide-format route closed 17-Apr-2026. Indian HRC: nothing. THAT IS THE MECHANISM - the ministry closed the Chinese channel and, in the same document a year earlier, explicitly left the Indian one open. AND IT CREATES A FORWARD ITEM, STATED WITH ITS UNCERTAINTY. The termination rests on a threshold that is volume-dependent and dated. IF Indian volumes have since risen above 3% of imports, the ground for termination has eroded and a fresh petition becomes possible - and HPG is already a proven petitioner, twice. WHETHER INDIAN VOLUMES NOW EXCEED 3% IS NOT ESTABLISHED HERE AND IS NOT ASSUMED. This is recorded as a mechanism to watch, not as a prediction. The cheap check is Indian HRC's share of Vietnamese HRC imports in 2026. A TRAP DISARMED BY INTERNAL LOGIC RATHER THAN BY COUNTING SOURCES. One source gives the wide-format band as 1,800-2,300mm; the others give 1,880-2,300mm. THE UNDERLYING DUTY COVERS WIDTHS BELOW 1,880mm, so an anti-circumvention band starting at 1,800mm would OVERLAP the existing measure by 80mm, which is incoherent - an anti-circumvention measure exists precisely to catch what falls OUTSIDE the original scope. 1,880 IS RIGHT AND 1,800 IS A TYPO. Note the method: the majority-of-sources heuristic would have reached the same answer here, but the logical test is the one that would still work if the typo had been the majority. NOTHING MODELLED; no confidence moved. No model input changed - the bridge's HRC input is HPG's own offer, which embeds all of this by construction.
